name: Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd
title: Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd - 517334 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record FY26 revenue above INR 1.25 lakh crore (+11%) and leverage at an all-time low 0.8x, but capex of INR 6,000 crore planned for FY27 keeps supply expanding; the consumer electronics ramp is still unproven, with GF3 the key test.

triggers.label: FY27 capex ~INR 6,000 Cr
triggers.quote: For FY27, we expect capex of approximately INR 6,000 Crores plus/minus 10%

triggers.label: Leverage 0.8x, all-time low
triggers.quote: our leverage ratio improved further and reached an all -time low of 0.8x

triggers.label: GF3 utilisation zero, start-up
triggers.quote: the third plant utilization is zero right now because it's in start -up phase

triggers.label: Aerospace order book +20% to USD 1.6B
triggers.quote: The order book increased by over 20% to USD1.6 Billion

summary.headline: Motherson posted record Q4 FY26 revenue up 17% YoY, with EBITDA up 42% and margin up 200 bps, and FY27 capex guided at about INR 6,000 Cr.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the highest-ever quarterly revenue, growing 17% YoY, with EBITDA up 42% and margins up 200 bps YoY, aided by lighting & electronics and aerospace. Normalized PAT rose 66% in Q4, while reported PAT absorbed INR 177 Cr post-tax of European transformation provisions. FY26 revenue crossed INR 1.25 Lakh Cr (+11%), EBITDA margin was 9.5%, and leverage fell to an all-time low of 0.8x. Management flagged copper up about 38% YoY and Middle East-linked crude and polymer inflation, with pass-through recovery expected to lag one or two quarters.

financial_highlights.value: Growth of 42% YoY; margin expanded 200 bps
Grew 66% (reported PAT after INR 177 Cr post-tax Europe provisions)
Growth of 17% (reported PAT includes INR 328 Cr Europe adjustments, ~INR 25 Cr Labour Code impact, ~INR 45 Cr accelerated amortization, all post-tax)
USD 22.9 Billion; FY25 restated to USD 21.2 Billion at INR 84.55/USD
All-time high USD 96 Billion; ~22% EV, ~3% non-automotive
Capex INR 5,911 Cr (49% of EBITDA); net leverage 0.8x; ROCE 16.1%

segments.name: Consumer electronics
segments.commentary: Revenue grew about 7.5x YoY in FY26 and about 46% QoQ in Q4; achieved EBITDA profitability in FY26 and Q4 run rate in line with 14-16 million unit annual guidance from GF1 and GF2.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 40% YoY (roughly INR 2,400 Cr per analyst reference), with order book up over 20% to USD 1.6 Billion; two new Indian facilities expected in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Wiring harness
segments.commentary: Margin expanded about 170 bps QoQ despite copper; management attributed it to operational improvements in global entities, with a copper lag to be recovered.

segments.name: Lighting & electronics / emerging businesses
segments.commentary: Revenue growth about 30% per analyst; margin improvement cited as a driver of group margin expansion, with GF3 expected to be the main step-up.

segments.name: Precision metal & modules
segments.commentary: Growth of 2.7x, largely from the Atsumitec acquisition, per analyst question; management highlighted machining as a core focus.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at about INR 6,000 Cr (plus/minus 10%), split 50% growth and 50% maintenance; growth capex skewed to consumer electronics.
Consumer electronics GF3 facility (largest, 33 football fields) on track for commissioning in Q3 FY27; management declined to give revenue per unit.
Nexans automotive harness acquisition expected to close end-June/early-July 2026; Yutaka Giken acquisition expected by end of H1 FY27.
Dividend of INR 0.25 final, INR 0.60 total for FY26 (16.4% payout); Vision 2030 targets USD 108 Billion gross revenue and 40% ROCE over time.
Management expects ROCE to improve progressively; expects customer pass-through of copper and energy costs with a one to two quarter lag.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR 5,911 Cr; FY27 guided at about INR 6,000 Cr ±10%.
16 facilities under development globally, 13 scheduled to come on stream in FY27; 4 new facilities announced (2 wiring harness, 2 logistics); all 16 in emerging markets.

Consumer electronics GF3 utilisation is zero during start-up; management said it will be above or in line with budget. Capex for the business for the current year is being finalised, expected broadly in line with last year's INR 2,600 Cr guidance, firm numbers in one quarter.
Aerospace: two new Indian plants expected in Q1 FY27 to serve the USD 1.6 Billion order book.
demand_pricing: Order book USD 96 Billion, diversified across PV, CV, off-highway, rolling stock and 2-wheelers; emerging economies rising share.

Cost pass-through: contractual for some customers, negotiated for others; lag of one to two quarters. Q4 impact of Middle East-linked costs was limited to a few weeks; Q1 FY27 costs largely expected to be recovered over time.
Europe: new OEM launches in FY27 and content-heavy wins cited; restructuring under way in Central and Western Europe.
Consumer electronics order visibility is short-cycle (about 1 year); management did not confirm a USD 1.4 Billion FY28 execution figure but said targets are plus/minus 10% of analyst-derived numbers.
Aerospace order cycle about 5-8 years per management; automotive orders run 2-3 years to execution.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for Integrated Assemblies (MSAS) in FY27, given new program launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects meaningful growth driven by program wins and diversification, but declined to guide numbers as it depends on customer vehicle sales.

qa_highlights.question: Is cost pass-through for overheads and polymers contractual or negotiated?
qa_highlights.answer: Depends on customer: a mix of contracted and negotiated arrangements; some customers show a lag, and new units are now covering fixed costs.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer electronics utilisation and top-20 customers?
qa_highlights.answer: GF1 and GF2 are fully used; GF3 utilisation is zero until commissioning in Q3 FY27. Consumer electronics customers fall under "others" and are not disclosed by name.

qa_highlights.question: Nexans deal timing and debt exposure to rising yields?
qa_highlights.answer: Nexans closing expected end-June/early-July 2026. Debt is a mix of fixed and floating; management said net debt/EBITDA is at a low and will keep falling.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue per unit for consumer electronics and EBITDA contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide revenue per unit until GF3 scales; agreed the contribution to lighting & electronics EBITDA is currently small.

qa_highlights.question: Aerospace order book duration and growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book of USD 1.6 Billion (up from USD 1.2 Billion last reported) is expected to execute over about 5-8 years, front-ended; no quantified FY27 growth guidance.

risks_watch: Copper (up about 38% YoY in Q4) and crude/polymer inflation, with pass-through lags of one to two quarters and Q1 FY27 cost exposure.
Consumer electronics ramp depends on GF3 commissioning in Q3 FY27 and customer order flow; no revenue-per-unit disclosure yet.
European volume weakness and further restructuring costs; reported PAT hit by Europe provisions (INR 328 Cr in FY26).
Interest-rate exposure on floating-rate debt; ROCE fell to 16.1% from 17.2% amid record capex.
Nexans closing timing and integration; pipeline of acquisitions could raise leverage above the current 0.8x.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, aerospace and consumer electronics, but guarded on specifics: management repeatedly declined to give numbers on consumer electronics revenue per unit, MSAS growth and FY28 execution. It was cautious on cost pass-through timing and European volumes.
key_quotes: Q4 FY 26 was our highest ever revenue quarter with revenues growing 17% year -on-year.
GF3 is the largest facility that we will have in Motherson. It's a size of 33 football fields that is going to come into commission.
For us, top line is vanity, bottom line is sanity, cash in the bank is reality.

adds.what: Consumer electronics GF3 facility (largest, 33 football fields)
16 facilities under development globally, 13 scheduled to come on stream in FY27
Two new Indian aerospace plants serving USD 1.6B order book

growth.why: FY27 capex guided at ~INR 6,000 Cr ±10% (50% growth), with 13 of 16 facilities under development due in FY27 and an all-time-high USD 96B order book, though no explicit FY27 revenue growth number was given and GF3 is only due in Q3 FY27.
